reasoning: A May 2026 preprint (arXiv 2605.06327, "Measuring Evaluation-Context Divergence in Open-Weight LLMs: A Paired-Prompt Protocol") implements essentially this exact proposal: a paired-prompt protocol measuring within-item behavioral divergence between evaluation, deployment, and neutral framings on a fixed task set, run on 5 open-weight instruct checkpoints across 4 families (incl. Llama-3.1, Mistral), scored on refusal and harmful-compliance with LLM-judge cross-checks (two judges) and significance testing, while explicitly controlling for paraphrase variation and judge framing-sensitivity — and it argues framing-controlled A/B prompts should become standard evaluation infrastructure. The broader problem (whether models behave differently when they detect evaluation, and quantifying the eval-vs-deployment gap) is also covered by Needham et al. (2505.23836, "LLMs Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated"), the Hawthorne-effect test-awareness work (2505.14617), the GPT-OSS-20B eval-awareness study (2510.08624), and the open-weight scaling paper (2509.13333). The proposal's deltas — ~40 vs 20 items, naturalistic email/chat embedding, added effort/hedging metrics, and emphasis on a packaged community-release battery — are incremental refinements over already-published paired-prompt protocols rather than a new problem or method.

evidence.title: Measuring Evaluation-Context Divergence in Open-Weight LLMs: A Paired-Prompt Protocol with Pilot Evidence of Alignment-Pipeline-Specific Heterogeneity
evidence.summary: Near-identical to the proposal: defines a paired-prompt protocol measuring within-item behavior change under evaluation vs deployment vs neutral framing on a fixed task set; 20 paired items across 5 open-weight instruct checkpoints from 4 families (Llama-3.1, Mistral-Small, Phi-3.5, OLMo-3), 840 generations/checkpoint; metrics are refusal rate and harmful compliance with two LLM-judge classifiers (incl. Llama-Guard-3) and significance testing; controls for paraphrase and judge framing-sensitivity; argues framing-controlled A/B prompts should be standard deployment-evaluation practice.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated (Needham et al.)
evidence.summary: Establishes the core problem: frontier and open models can classify transcripts as evaluation vs deployment and sometimes infer the test purpose, framing eval-awareness as a distribution shift threatening evaluation validity.

evidence.title: The Hawthorne Effect in Reasoning Models: Evaluating and Steering Test Awareness
evidence.summary: Measures and steers behavioral change induced by test-awareness in reasoning models, directly addressing the eval-vs-deployment behavioral-gap measurement problem.

evidence.title: Do LLMs Know They Are Being Tested? Evaluation Awareness and Incentive-Sensitive Failures in GPT-OSS-20B
evidence.summary: Uses paired prompts signaling evaluation vs deployment on an open-weight model (GPT-OSS-20B) and measures behavior divergence across task categories, an instance of the same measurement approach the proposal describes.

evidence.title: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Documents evaluation awareness specifically in open-weight LLMs and its power-law scaling with model size, covering the open-weight focus of the proposal.
